{"milestones": [{"id": "m1", "title": "Add run_postprocessors, render_inner_html, and striptags to toc module", "requests": ["R7", "R3"], "requirement": "The toc extension must expose three new public helper functions so that third-party extensions can process heading content without relying on the deprecated get_name and stashedHTML2text. striptags must convert an HTML string to plain text without unescaping HTML entities (unlike markupsafe's implementation).", "observable": "Calling markdown.extensions.toc.striptags('

Hello & world

') returns 'Hello & world' (entities preserved, not unescaped). Calling markdown.extensions.toc.render_inner_html(md, elem) returns the serialized inner HTML of elem. Calling markdown.extensions.toc.run_postprocessors(md, text) returns the text after all md.postprocessors have been applied. All three are importable from markdown.extensions.toc.", "public_names": ["run_postprocessors", "render_inner_html", "striptags"], "requires": [], "why_requires": ""}, {"id": "m2", "title": "Use new helpers in TocTreeprocessor.run to process heading content", "requests": ["R1", "R2"], "requirement": "TocTreeprocessor.run must call run_postprocessors on heading content so all postprocessors are applied (fixing footnote-reference leakage into TOC entries), and must use striptags (via render_inner_html) instead of the deprecated get_name/stashedHTML2text to obtain the plain-text heading name.", "observable": "Converting '# Header with footnote[^1]\\n\\n[^1]: text' with extensions=['toc','footnotes'] produces a TOC whose link text is 'Header with footnote' (the footnote ref number '1' is stripped). The toc_tokens entry for that heading has name == 'Header with footnote' and html does not contain the footnote sup element. No call to get_name or stashedHTML2text is needed; the code path goes through run_postprocessors and striptags.", "public_names": ["TocTreeprocessor.run", "run_postprocessors", "striptags", "render_inner_html"], "requires": ["m1"], "why_requires": "TocTreeprocessor.run calls run_postprocessors and striptags which are the public functions added in m1; without them the heading-content pipeline cannot replace get_name/stashedHTML2text."}, {"id": "m3", "title": "Save name/html/data-toc-label tokens and unescape before slugify", "requests": ["R4", "R5", "R6"], "requirement": "Each toc_tokens entry must contain the plain-text 'name', the rich 'html' (inner HTML of the heading), and the raw unescaped 'data-toc-label' attribute value. The data-toc-label must be sanitized through striptags before being written to name, separate from the heading-content pipeline. An html.unescape call must be made immediately before slugify so slugify operates on Unicode, but html.unescape must NOT be applied to name, html, or data-toc-label.", "observable": "For a heading '# Foo & Bar' with data-toc-label attribute set to 'Custom & Label', the corresponding toc_tokens entry has name == 'Custom & Label' (entities preserved, not unescaped), html contains the rendered heading markup, and data-toc-label == 'Custom & Label'. The generated id/slug is derived from html.unescape of the label (so '&' becomes '&' before slugify), yielding e.g. 'custom-label'. Converting with markdown.extensions.toc and inspecting md.toc_tokens confirms all three keys are present.", "public_names": ["TocTreeprocessor.run", "toc_tokens", "striptags", "render_inner_html", "run_postprocessors"], "requires": ["m2"], "why_requires": "m3 extends the heading-processing pipeline established in m2: the 'name' token value is produced by the striptags+run_postprocessors path wired up in m2, and the 'html' token value comes from render_inner_html called within that same m2 pipeline; m3 adds the token-saving and slugify-unescape steps on top of it."}], "expected_causes": ["striptags might accidentally unescape HTML entities (e.g. using html.unescape internally), violating R3's requirement that entities are preserved.", "run_postprocessors might skip some postprocessors or fail to handle AtomicString inputs correctly.", "The footnote-ref stripping in m2 might only work for the default footnote format and miss edge cases like multiple refs or nested footnotes.", "In m3, html.unescape might be applied to name/html/data-toc-label values instead of only before slugify, breaking R6's constraint.", "data-toc-label sanitization might reuse the heading-content pipeline instead of running striptags separately, causing double-processing or missing the raw value in the token.", "toc_tokens structure might omit one of the three keys (name, html, data-toc-label) or store them under different names."], "verifier_plan": "m1: unit tests import striptags, render_inner_html, run_postprocessors from markdown.extensions.toc; assert striptags('

A & B

') == 'A & B' (no unescape); assert run_postprocessors returns text processed through md.postprocessors; assert render_inner_html returns serialized children. m2: convert '# H[^1]\\n\\n[^1]: f' with toc+footnotes; assert the TOC
  • link text is 'H' (no trailing '1'); assert toc_tokens[0]['name'] == 'H'; assert no footnote sup appears in the TOC HTML. m3: convert a heading with data-toc-label='Custom & Label'; assert toc_tokens[0] has keys 'name','html','data-toc-label'; assert name == 'Custom & Label' (entities kept); assert data-toc-label == 'Custom & Label'; assert the generated id is 'custom-label' (html.unescape applied before slugify); assert html field contains the rich inner markup."}

Let me analyze the requests and code links to find related milestones that build on each other.

Looking at the requests, R1-R7 all relate to the TOC extension's handling of heading content. Let me trace the dependencies:

- R7: Deprecates `get_name` and `stashedHTML2text`, introduces `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html`, and `striptags` as replacements.
- R1: All postprocessors are now run on heading content (this uses `run_postprocessors`).
- R2: Footnote references are stripped from heading content (uses `striptags` or similar).
- R3: A more robust `striptags` is provided to convert headings to plain text. Unlike markupsafe, HTML entities are not unescaped.
- R4: The plain text `name`, rich `html`, and unescaped raw `data-toc-label` are saved to `toc_tokens`.
- R5: The value of `data-toc-label` is sanitized separate from heading content before being written to `name`.
- R6: An `html.unescape` call is made just prior to calling `slugify`.

The code links show:
- `get_name` calls `unescape` (in toc.py)
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `get_name`, `slugify`, `stashedHTML2text`, `unescape`
- `slugify_unicode` calls `slugify`

So the dependency chain is:
1. First, we need `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html`, and `striptags` (R7) - these are new public functions.
2. Then, `TocTreeprocessor.run` uses these new functions instead of `get_name`/`stashedHTML2text` (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6).

Let me pick milestones that are truly dependent:

M1: Introduce `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html`, and `striptags` as public functions in the toc module (R7). These are the foundation.

M2: Use `run_postprocessors` and `striptags` in `TocTreeprocessor.run` to process heading content, replacing `get_name` and `stashedHTML2text`. Also implement R1 (all postprocessors run on heading content) and R2 (footnote refs stripped). This depends on M1 because it calls `run_postprocessors` and `striptags`.

M3: Implement R4, R5, R6 - save `name`, `html`, and `data-toc-label` to `toc_tokens`, sanitize `data-toc-label` separately, and add `html.unescape` before `slugify`. This depends on M2 because the heading processing pipeline established in M2 is what produces the tokens.

Wait, let me reconsider. R3 says `striptags` should NOT unescape HTML entities (unlike markupsafe). R6 says `html.unescape` is called just prior to `slugify` but NOT on `name`, `html`, or `data-toc-label`. These are related.

Let me structure:

M1: Add `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html`, `striptags` public functions (R7, R3).
- `striptags` converts HTML to plain text but does NOT unescape entities.
- `run_postprocessors` runs all postprocessors on content.
- `render_inner_html` renders inner HTML of an element.

M2: Use these in `TocTreeprocessor.run` to build `toc_tokens` with `name`, `html`, `data-toc-label` (R1, R2, R4, R5, R6).
- R1: postprocessors run on heading content (uses `run_postprocessors` from M1)
- R2: footnote refs stripped (uses `striptags` from M1)
- R4: tokens contain `name`, `html`, `data-toc-label`
- R5: `data-toc-label` sanitized separately before writing to `name`
- R6: `html.unescape` before `slugify` only

This is a natural 2-milestone split. Let me check if there's a third that makes sense.

Actually, R1 and R2 could be separate from R4/R5/R6. Let me think about whether they're truly dependent on each other or on M1.

- M2a: `TocTreeprocessor.run` uses `run_postprocessors` (R1) and `striptags` (R2, R3) to get plain text heading content. This replaces `get_name`/`stashedHTML2text`.
- M2b: `TocTreeprocessor.run` saves `name`, `html`, `data-toc-label` to `toc_tokens` (R4, R5, R6). This builds on the heading processing from M2a.

So three milestones:
- m1: New public functions (R7, R3)
- m2: Use them in TocTreeprocessor.run for heading content processing (R1, R2) - depends on m1
- m3: Save tokens with name/html/data-toc-label, sanitize separately, unescape before slugify (R4, R5, R6) - depends on m2

Let me verify the code_links support these dependencies:
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `get_name` → in m2, this is replaced by `run_postprocessors`/`striptags`
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `stashedHTML2text` → deprecated, replaced
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `slugify` → in m3, `html.unescape` is added before this
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `unescape` → related to m3's handling

The dependency chain is real: m2 calls functions added in m1, and m3 builds on the heading processing pipeline established in m2.

Let me finalize:

m1: Add `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html`, `striptags` (R7, R3)
m2: Replace `get_name`/`stashedHTML2text` usage in `TocTreeprocessor.run` with new functions; run postprocessors on heading content; strip footnote refs (R1, R2) - requires m1
m3: Save `name`, `html`, `data-toc-label` to `toc_tokens`; sanitize `data-toc-label` separately; `html.unescape` before `slugify` (R4, R5, R6) - requires m2

For m2's why_requires: `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `run_postprocessors` and `striptags` which are added in m1.
For m3's why_requires: m3 builds on the heading content processing pipeline established in m2, where `render_inner_html` (from m1, used in m2) produces the `html` token value, and `striptags` (from m1, used in m2) produces the `name` token value.

Actually, m3 also depends on m1 for `render_inner_html` and `striptags`. But the primary dependency is on m2 because m2 establishes the processing pipeline that m3 extends with token saving.

Let me write the milestones carefully.
